tasks.short: Conduct environmental research and publish checked scientific findings.

steps.what: Design the environmental research question, methods and analysis plan
Conduct research observations and collect environmental evidence
Record environmental research observations, sources and methodological departures
Calculate predefined research summaries and figures
Interpret research findings and define defensible publication claims
Write and check the research manuscript against sources and results

loop.purpose: Draft publication prose from the researcher's chosen claims and evidence.
loop.input: Outline, findings, limitations, source passages and identified results.
loop.output: Draft manuscript with source anchors and explicit evidence gaps.
loop.check: Researcher checks every substantive claim, number and citation and revises the complete manuscript.
loop.stop: One revision; unsupported sections are written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template cannot explain varied environmental findings.

steps.what: Submit or publish the exact final research manuscript

tasks.design: Use native research capture in {SPREADSHEET}, tested summaries in {DATA_PLATFORM} and a bounded manuscript draft in {DOCS}. The researcher chooses methods and claims, checks the complete text and separately submits or publishes it through {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research records, repeated summaries and first manuscript prose are prepared manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Checked data and explicit claims can support repeat calculations and constrained drafting.
tasks.still_hard: Environmental confounding and uncertain evidence require scientific judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Determine what the research establishes and what it does not.

ambition.what: Inspect another predefined comparison before finalising the interpretation.

tasks.altitude: Reduce repetitive preparation while keeping research conclusions accountable.

reach.learn: Keep units, source identity and protocol departures explicit.

evidence.claim: Native capture, tested analysis and source-bounded drafting could reduce repeated research preparation; this labour estimate is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Research capture, analysis, interpretation, manuscript writing and publication are inside the task and separately counted.

The researcher produces observation or source identifier, date, variable, value, units, method and caveat in s3, with eight retained hours including capture. The s1 design defines summaries. Missing or incompatible inputs stop analysis for manual investigation in s5.

The researcher produces claims and outline in s5 and selects reference passages in s6; its 12 retained hours include source selection, drafting checks and revision. Unsupported references are omitted or completed manually.
Try native records and analysis tools first. Calculations earn savings only where currently prepared manually; internal author revision has no self-approval gate.
unknowns: Research methods and current analysis automation.
research_questions: Does the workflow reduce total research and manuscript time after validation and full source checking?

already_counted.description: Check and revise source-based manuscript drafting.

incremental.description: Maintain capture structures, analysis tests and draft checks.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final manuscript, figures, attachments and publication destination; changes require a fresh submission-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=75, gross=25; upkeep=5 gives central net=20. Research judgement and field observation retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain attendance and grade records with checked transfer between systems.

steps.what: Capture student attendance and other required source records
Collect examiner-set grades and identify their assessment versions
Map attendance and grades to the destination student records
Verify the exact student record batch against source evidence
Write the verified batch into the destination student records
Reconcile the import receipt and correct outstanding student record errors

tasks.design: Configure native attendance fields in {LMS} and supported mapping into the student register in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Keep capture and exact-batch verification human, then separately import the verified batch and reconcile the receipt.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attendance and examiner-set grades are copied into another required student register.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable student and assessment identifiers support a checked deterministic transfer.
tasks.still_hard: The wrong student or assessment version can make an otherwise accurate value incorrect.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve record conflicts and preserve the examiner's actual decision.
tasks.altitude: Keep required student records consistent without re-deciding grades.

reach.learn: Reconcile import receipts against exact student and assessment identifiers.

evidence.claim: The digest reports Radboud's requirement to publish Brightspace grades in OSIRIS as well, illustrating a real double-recording boundary.
Native capture and a checked transfer could reduce duplicate record work; the labour saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: This scenario has a separate required destination register. Grade setting and student result release belong to task 5901; this task owns only required record capture and transfer.

The teacher produces student identifier, class date, attendance status and required facts in s1, with 20 retained hours including capture. The examiner produces the grade result in task 5901; collection and version selection are fully counted in s2.

The teacher supplies destination mapping definitions during setup. Missing identity, disputed grade or unmatched assessment stops the affected write and requires manual correction in s4. Only the verified batch version can be imported.
Use native export/import first. The gate checks transfer accuracy of a second-system write, not an author's same-system save; no model evaluates students.
unknowns: Supported interfaces and whether a duplicate required register actually exists.
research_questions: Can the transfer preserve student and assessment identity and prevent superseded grades from being imported?

already_counted.description: Verify the exact batch and resolve record mismatches.

incremental.description: Maintain mapping definitions and regression-check imports.

approvals.approved_version: Exact batch identifier, student identifiers, assessment versions, attendance statuses and grade values verified in s4; any change invalidates the batch verification.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 duplicate-register scenario: B=100, R=60, gross=40; upkeep=8 gives central net=32. Existing native synchronisation reduces the gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile and administer examinations and set checked grades using native assessment tools.

steps.what: Define examination coverage, question types and marking criteria
Compile examination questions and enter the checked closed-question answer key
Release the final examination version to the intended students
Administer examinations and monitor completion under the assessment arrangements
Calculate closed-question scores from the checked answer key
Grade open examination responses against the marking criteria
Check scoring exceptions and set the final examination results
Release the final examination results to the correct students

tasks.design: Configure native item-bank and closed-question scoring in {LMS}, using the blueprint in {DOCS}. The examiner writes and checks questions, administers the examination, grades open responses, sets results and separately releases each final version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Question preparation and closed-question score calculation repeat structured work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native item banks and answer-key scoring can handle those bounded parts.
tasks.still_hard: Assessment validity, open responses and exceptional circumstances require an examiner.
tasks.human_edge: Judge demonstrated understanding and resolve ambiguous or unfair scoring.
tasks.altitude: Keep assessment decisions human while reducing repeated preparation and arithmetic.

reach.learn: Preserve response identity and report administration exceptions.

evidence.claim: Ans supports automatic closed-question marking, open-question allocation and item statistics.
The digest describes examiners as responsible for setting results; the design retains that decision.

assumptions: This scenario has a mixed examination with reusable items and closed questions. No AI grading, proctoring or fraud decision is proposed.

The teacher produces item versions, response options, correct answers and point values in s2, with 17.5 retained hours including capture and checks. Students produce responses during s4, whose full administration time is counted. Missing or invalid response mappings go to manual resolution in s7.
The teacher acts as the appointed examiner in s7. Official result transfer into another required register belongs to task 5904 and is counted once there.
Use native assessment settings first. Internal question or grade writing has no author self-approval gate; exact-version checks occur at the two real releases.
unknowns: Share of closed questions and current use of native scoring and item banks.
research_questions: Can native scoring reproduce known answer-key scores and expose response-mapping exceptions before result release?

already_counted.description: Check score exceptions and set final results.

incremental.description: Maintain item keys and regression-check scoring and release settings.

approvals.approved_version: Exact examination version, cohort and release timing; any change requires another release-time check.
Exact examiner-set result batch and each student's result visibility; changed grades or identity mapping require a fresh release check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 mixed-exam scenario: B=100, R=77.5, gross=22.5; upkeep=5 gives central net=17.5. Existing auto-marking would reduce the opportunity.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain office hours, advise students and record necessary follow-up.

steps.what: Set regularly scheduled office hours and availability
Publish the final office-hour availability to students
Retrieve relevant course requirements and prior student follow-up
Listen to students and clarify their assistance needs
Advise and assist students during the scheduled office hours
Write necessary student follow-up actions and relevant advice notes

tasks.design: Keep office hours and live advice human. Configure a native course-reference view in {LMS} and {DOCS}, plus concise follow-up fields; publish availability separately from setting it in {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Course lookups and repeated follow-up record structure interrupt advice work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference links and concise action fields can reduce clerical effort.
tasks.still_hard: Students' needs and circumstances require attention and responsive judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the concern and offer applicable advice rather than a generic answer.
tasks.altitude: Keep the teacher present while making necessary follow-up easier to maintain.

reach.learn: Record only necessary actions and distinguish advice from an official decision.

evidence.claim: Native course views and concise follow-up templates could reduce lookup and repeated writing; this office-hour saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: This scenario includes necessary follow-up notes for substantive advice cases; it does not require a new record of every casual student conversation.

The teacher produces student identifier, date, relevant advice, agreed action and due date in s6, with 10.5 retained hours including capture and checks. Unknown facts stay unresolved and receive manual clarification.
Use native course links and fields first. No chatbot, recording, automated referral or generated advice is proposed.
Internal notes have no self-approval gate or save-time saving. Publication and live advice have checks on the exact content communicated.
unknowns: Actual volume of necessary follow-up writing and existing templates.
research_questions: Does the native view and note structure reduce clerical work without expanding unnecessary student data capture?

already_counted.description: Write and check necessary follow-up notes.

incremental.description: Maintain course links and follow-up fields.

approvals.approved_version: Exact office-hour dates, times, location and course audience; changes require another publication-time check.
Each exact advice statement and agreed action communicated to this student; new advice is checked for applicability before expression.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 follow-up scenario: B=100, R=93.5, gross=6.5; upkeep=1.5 gives central net=5. Office presence and advice time remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep research, assessment and student advice accountable while reducing repeated records and preparation.
reach: Connect checked research, examination decisions and consistent student records.
role.ambitious_version: An environmental science teacher who spends more time on evidence, learning and student needs while keeping records traceable.
